# [CS002] OS Command Injection (command-injection)

A process is started with a command line built from untrusted data.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html) |
| **OWASP** | A05:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Passing input to sh -c lets shell metacharacters (;, |, $()) run arbitrary commands. Even without a shell, a user-chosen executable or a leading - in an argument changes what runs. Run a fixed executable, pass input as separate arguments after --, and validate it against an allowlist.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func convert(r *http.Request) error {
	name := r.FormValue("file")
	return exec.Command("sh", "-c", "convert "+name+" out.png").Run()
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func convert(r *http.Request) error {
	name := filepath.Base(r.FormValue("file"))
	if !validName.MatchString(name) {
		return errInvalidName
	}
	return exec.CommandContext(r.Context(), "convert", "--", name, "out.png").Run()
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [command-injection]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    command-injection: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore command-injection -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** command-injection
```
